name: Las Vegas Sands Corp.
moat_justification: Singapore duopoly and unmatched Macau scale are real and hard to replicate, but the moat is a government licence, not owned property: concessions are time-limited and repriced at renewal with mandated non-gaming spend (Macau plan ~$4.44B through 2032), and Macau customers have no switching costs, so premium-mass share is defended with reinvestment that is compressing margins. MBS earns ~50% property EBITDA margins as one of only two licensed Singapore resorts; against that, the entire asset base sits in two jurisdictions exposed to Chinese consumer health, capital controls, and hold luck.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Premier Asia casino cash machine (Singapore duopoly + Macau scale), moat 6/10 — clears 15% only on the TTM base (17.7% weighted, IV $47.00 vs $37.89); on the median base it is a C (12.8%, IV $30.71), which is also the price that clears 15% with a margin of safety.
moat_for: Singapore duopoly: one of only two licensed IRs, MBS dominant with ~50%+ property EBITDA margins
Largest Macau footprint: five properties, unmatched Cotai scale across segments
Iconic irreplicable assets (Marina Bay Sands, Venetian/Londoner cluster)
moat_against: Moat is a time-limited government concession, repriced at renewal with mandated non-gaming capex
Zero customer switching costs in Macau: six concessionaires in a premium-mass reinvestment war, margins compressing
Total concentration in two jurisdictions exposed to China policy, capital controls, consumer health
Hold-luck volatility: low rolling hold cut Q2 2026 Macau EBITDA by ~$87M vs normalized
